name: bs_plugin
stressor: BREADTH / plugins: a value that exists ONLY behind a plugin-registered tool. setup() writes a sliceagent plugin (workdir/.sliceagent/plugins/releasekit/{plugin.toml,__init__.py}) whose register(ctx) calls ctx.register_tool('get_release_token', handler=...) returning an unguessable magic token RT-7731-<random hex>. The harness's BREADTH wiring (meta.plugins=true) runs load_plugins(tools.registry, skills_mgr, [workdir/.sliceagent/plugins], root=workdir) so the tool is live in the registry the loop drives.
source_note: The plugin's __init__.py register(ctx) registers get_release_token with a handler that returns a token whose random suffix is persisted to workdir/.sliceagent/plugins/releasekit/.token at setup time. The token is NOT written anywhere the agent reads as plain data and is NOT in the prompt — the ONLY way to obtain it is to invoke the plugin tool. Reference fix reads that persisted token and writes it to release.txt, simulating an agent that called the tool.
discriminator: Success PROVES the plugin mechanism was used: the oracle requires release.txt to contain the EXACT magic token the plugin tool returns, which is unguessable and unobtainable except by calling get_release_token. A no-op setup (token never written to release.txt) FAILS; only an agent that actually invokes the plugin-registered tool can pass. Tests that load_plugins registers the tool into the registry the loop drives.
